title: TreeMap 2020, 2022, and 2023: Improved species range mapping in a tree-level forest dataset for the conterminous United States
abstract:
New TreeMap datasets provide imputed 30 m gridded maps with modeled tree-level detail for forests across the conterminous United States in 2020, 2022, and 2023. Updated methods improve climate data inputs, independent validation approaches, and species range mapping. These improvements strengthen TreeMap’s use in Earth system applications such as carbon cycling, wildfire behavior, and habitat distribution modeling, which depend on accurate representations of forest composition and structure. 
 TreeMap is a tree-level model of the forests of the conterminous United States (CONUS) that provides a spatially continuous, 30 m resolution representation of forest structure and composition. It uses a random forests imputation approach to assign the most similar Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) plot to each forested pixel in gridded LANDFIRE data based on a suite of predictor variables that include vegetation, topographic, biophysical, and disturbance characteristics. By linking every mapped pixel to an FIA plot identifier for all forested areas in CONUS, TreeMap bridges localized inventory measurements with national-scale analyses and provides high-resolution estimates of forest structure and composition. In this update, TreeMap 2020, 2022, and 2023 incorporate climatic variables from Daymet in place of LANDFIRE biophysical variables. Further, we refined the independent validation by limiting the analysis to FIA plots where heterogeneity was administrative rather than ecological, excluding plots previously used to validate TreeMap versions that spanned heterogeneous forest conditions.  TreeMap 2020, 2022, and 2023 also implement a new process constraining the pool of FIA plots available for imputation within each LANDFIRE zone to species documented within that zone and its adjacent zones, thereby reducing implausible species assignments across CONUS. TreeMap 2020, 2022, and 2023 are publicly available at https://doi.org/10.2737/RDS-2025-0031 (Zimmer et al., 2025) and https://doi.org/10.2737/RDS-2025-0032 (Houtman et al., 2025), and https://doi.org/10.2737/RDS-2026-0038 (Zimmer et al., 2026), respectively.

title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability
abstract:
A method developed to directly measure fungal melanin in soil, reveals a strong link between melanin and soil carbon and providing evidence for its role in long-term carbon stabilization 
 Fungal necromass, particularly dead microbial cells rich in melanin, is an important contributor to long-term soil carbon stabilization. Progress in understanding the role of soil melanin is limited by the lack of validated analytical methods. DNA-based approaches estimate only the genetic potential for melanin production and therefore provide indirect evidence of melanin occurrence. To directly assess soil melanin, we evaluated spectroscopic and spectrophotometric assays; however, both approaches proved insufficiently specific due to interference from chemically related compounds. Here, we introduce a liquid chromatography method that enables quantification of major fungal melanin types in soils. By enabling direct quantification of fungal melanin in soil, this framework allows longstanding hypotheses regarding melanized fungal necromass and soil carbon stabilization to be tested mechanistically. Here, we show with the proposed method that soil melanin concentrations are strongly correlated with total soil carbon, supporting a central role for fungal melanin in long-term soil carbon stabilization. A method developed to directly measure fungal melanin in soil, reveals a strong link between melanin and soil carbon and providing evidence for its role in long-term carbon stabilization

title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
abstract:
Ocean drifter observations reveal that Atlantic near-inertial currents intensified by almost 4% per decade during 2003–2022. This intensification is primarily driven by changes in wind forcing associated with mesoscale weather systems. 
 Near-inertial currents (NICs) play a key role in surface material redistribution and ocean mixing, yet their long-term variability remains poorly known. Using in situ current measurements from surface drifters, we provide observational evidence for a pronounced intensification of surface NICs in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades (2003–2022). Basin–mean NIC strength increases at a rate of 3.8 ± 1.7% per decade, with a spatial pattern characterized by strengthening in the South Atlantic and the high-latitude North Atlantic, and weakening in the low-latitude North Atlantic. We further show that these trends in Atlantic NICs are primarily driven by changes in near-inertial wind forcing, particularly those associated with mesoscale weather systems, while variations in mixed-layer depth playing a minor role. This observed intensification of Atlantic NICs may have important implications for ocean transport and mixing, and needs to be properly represented in the current generation of climate models. Ocean drifter observations reveal that Atlantic near-inertial currents intensified by almost 4% per decade during 2003–2022. This intensification is primarily driven by changes in wind forcing associated with mesoscale weather systems.

title: HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
abstract:
Authors show in 2013-2023 France saw a substantial reduction in hepatitis C virus prevalence and incidence among people who use drugs. Widespread treatment and harm reduction drove the decline, bringing France closer to WHO 2030 elimination targets. 
 Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a key public health challenge, particularly among people who use and inject drugs (PWUD, PWID). While direct-acting antivirals (DAA) have revolutionized HCV treatment, meeting the WHO’s 2030 elimination target requires accurate estimation of incidence and prevalence to guide prevention and care. We analyze cross-sectional surveys conducted in France in 2004, 2013, and 2023, recruiting PWUD at harm reduction services and collecting behavioral and biological data. We estimate age-and time-dependent prevalence of HCV antibodies and HCV RNA using multivariate regression models while incidence was estimated from two-state transmission models. The demographic profile of PWUD has aged over time (mean age 35 years in 2004 vs. 44 in 2023) while injection prevalence remained stable (61.7% in 2023). Between 2013 and 2023, HCV burden declined substantially: HCV RNA prevalence fell from 19.4% (95% CI 16.3–23.0) to 9.5% (7.2–12.3) among all PWUD, and from 29.6% to 14.5% among PWID. Incidence among PWID decreased from 6.5 (4.1–8.0) to 2.4 (1.4–4.2) per 100 person-years. These reductions likely reflect the combined impact of DAA scale-up and harm reduction policies, marking substantial progress toward elimination targets. However, ongoing transmission highlights persistent barriers requiring targeted public health actions. Authors show in 2013-2023 France saw a substantial reduction in hepatitis C virus prevalence and incidence among people who use drugs. Widespread treatment and harm reduction drove the decline, bringing France closer to WHO 2030 elimination targets.

title: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
abstract:
Existing approaches for biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) discovery are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that an automated platform for one-step assembly and refactoring of BGCs facilitates facile novel product discovery. 
 Microbial genomes encode numerous biosynthetic gene clusters, yet most remain experimentally uncharacterized, particularly large non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) clusters that resist conventional cloning. Existing refactoring approaches are labor-intensive, depend on de novo DNA synthesis and are difficult to scale. Here we show that OSAR (One-Step Assembly and Refactoring)—an automated platform integrating algorithmic primer design with yeast homologous-recombination cloning—directly assembles and refactors NRPS clusters without custom DNA synthesis. We apply OSAR to 34 low- to medium-GC bacterial NRPS clusters (7–78 kb) and successfully assemble 31. Expression in Bacillus subtilis yields 29 peptides from 10 clusters. Several products arose from cryptic biosynthetic behaviors such as potential module skipping and premature release. OSAR provides a practical workflow for assembly and refactoring of NRPS clusters and may facilitate the translation of sequence information into natural products. title: In situ reduction-driven formation of sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures
abstract:
Sub-nanometer heterostructures offer opportunities to tune interfacial reactivity, but their precise construction remains challenging. Here, the authors report alternating Ni/NiMoO₄ heterostructures that promote hydrogen evolution and sustain durable high-current electrolysis. 
 Sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures provide a platform for modulating electronic structure and interfacial reactivity through strong atom-level coupling, with potential applications in energy conversion. However, their precise construction remains challenging. Here we show a strategy for constructing sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures through confined spinodal decomposition and ligand-mediated in situ reduction. Oleylamine ligands adsorbed on NiMoO4 sub-nanowires act as mild reductants, selectively reducing Ni2+ to spatially confined metallic Ni domains and forming coherent Ni/NiMoO4 heterointerfaces. Experimental and theoretical analyses suggest that the Ni/NiMoO4 interfaces modify the local electronic structure and facilitate the adsorption and activation of hydrogen evolution intermediates. The resulting catalyst requires an overpotential of 14.4 ± 2.9 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH and delivers 2 A cm−2 at 1.62 V in an anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer at 80 oC, with stable operation over 2200 h at 25 °C. These findings provide insights into the construction and interfacial regulation of sub-nanometer heterostructures through in situ reduction. Sub-nanometer heterostructures offer opportunities to tune interfacial reactivity, but their precise construction remains challenging. Here, the authors report alternating Ni/NiMoO₄ heterostructures that promote hydrogen evolution and sustain durable high-current electrolysis.

title: Asymmetric bloom lengthening drives high-latitude ocean chlorophyll accumulation imbalance
abstract:
This study shows that unequal changes in bloom duration between hemispheres contribute to contrasting high-latitude ocean chlorophyll trends, linking asymmetric phytoplankton phenology to marine ecosystem changes under climate warming. 
 Terrestrial ecosystems maintain a stable time-allocation budget between growth and senescence, but whether this applies to the ocean remains unclear. Using fused satellite LiDAR and ocean-color data (2007–2022), we show that marine phenology is variable and asymmetric. In high latitudes ( > 50°N), the bloom growth-to-decline ratio (RGD) is declining by ~5.3% per decade. While the chlorophyll-increase phase has lengthened by 2.3–5.5 days, the post-peak chlorophyll-decline phase has extended disproportionately by 5.7–6.2 days. Environmental sensitivity analyses reveal distinct hemispheric patterns in the statistical associations between phenological variability and multiple co-varying physical and biogeochemical factors, consistent with contrasting nutrient regimes between the Northern and Southern high-latitude oceans. We further show that these shifts are associated with spatially heterogeneous changes in marine chlorophyll accumulation patterns. Our results identify bloom asymmetry as an important dimension of marine phenological change, providing an observational baseline for evaluating future links between chlorophyll phenology, ecosystem timing, and polar biogeochemical processes under climate change. This study shows that unequal changes in bloom duration between hemispheres contribute to contrasting high-latitude ocean chlorophyll trends, linking asymmetric phytoplankton phenology to marine ecosystem changes under climate warming.

title: A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
abstract:
Adaptive radiations produce striking phenotypic diversity over remarkably short evolutionary timescales. This study uses genomic analyses of Darwin’s tree finches to reveal a cryptic lineage, in which autosomal differentiation with another sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus (G03) that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another. 
 Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin’s finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. Camarhynchus diversified over the last 100,000 years, yielding some striking morphological differences despite shallow genetic divergence. We identify several highly differentiated loci, including G03, a supergene affecting beak and body size. We reveal a striking example of genomic mosaicism, in which autosomal differentiation between two sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus -(G03)- that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another. Contextualized in a broader phylogenetic framework, we also reveal an unexpected diversity of G03 haplotypes and show that the small and large G03 alleles diverged early in the radiation, suggesting a key genetic innovation enabling ecological expansion among species of Darwin’s finches. Our results further establish Camarhynchus as a model example of speciation with gene flow, underscoring the broader role of hybridization in generating biodiversity. Adaptive radiations produce striking phenotypic diversity over remarkably short evolutionary timescales. This study uses genomic analyses of Darwin’s tree finches to reveal a cryptic lineage, in which autosomal differentiation with another sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus (G03) that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another.

title: Time-lapse RESOLFT nanoscopy empowered by deep learning
abstract:
The authors use two deep-learning methods for RESOLFT nanoscopy: HDN denoising enables five-fold longer live-cell imaging, while spatial upsampling with temporal context restores subsampled data for fourfold higher frame rates and reduced artifacts. 
 Capturing the dynamic interplay of proteins and organelles within cells requires microscopy methods with high spatial and temporal resolution. Reversible Saturable OpticaL Fluorescent Transition (RESOLFT) demonstrated great potential for live cell nanoscopy by using patterned light and reversibly switching fluorescent probes. Despite the latest improvement in both switching probes and optical schemes, the duration and frame rate of the time-lapse are still limited by photobleaching and spatial sampling steps. Here, we present two distinct strategies based on deep learning to restore low signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) or under-sampled images pushing the experimental boundaries of RESOLFT. We demonstrate the capability of Hierarchical DivNoising (HDN) to restore low-SNR RESOLFT data while maintaining full spatial resolution, both in supervised and unsupervised settings. This allows a 10-fold reduction of light dose per frame, and up to 5 times longer imaging. Then, we present Fast-MoNaLISA, a method that reduces the acquisition time of any point-scanning systems. This allows a 4-fold increase in frame rate, and a reduction of scanning artefacts. Overall, our methods open up possibilities for dynamic data acquisition at the sub-organelle level, such as vesicles budding in and out from intact mitochondria, or the actin meshwork formation and dissociation. The authors use two deep-learning methods for RESOLFT nanoscopy: HDN denoising enables five-fold longer live-cell imaging, while spatial upsampling with temporal context restores subsampled data for fourfold higher frame rates and reduced artifacts.

title: Recent change in northward migration of the East Asian summer front and increased compound wet–hot conditions
abstract:
Recent change in northward migration of the East Asian summer front and increased compound wet–hot conditions 
 The East Asian summer front (EASF) plays a key role in regional precipitation and heat stress, yet its long-term positional changes remain poorly understood. Using a front-tracking algorithm applied to ERA5 reanalysis (1979–2025), we identify northward migration of the EASF during both the active frontal season and late summer, with a more robust 1.92° shift in late summer. These shifts are associated with enhanced moisture transport, regional weakening of the upper-level jet, and localized sea surface temperature warming that has intensified and spatially broadened in recent decades. This poleward displacement is associated with increased frontal precipitation over Korea and enhanced heat stress across East Asia, with a greater likelihood of their co-occurrence, particularly during late summer. Our findings highlight frontal displacement as a pathway linking large-scale atmospheric and oceanic changes to regional climate risk and offer insight to inform climate projections and adaptation strategies over East Asia.

title: Tropical Indo-western Pacific forcing expedites warming in the northern Canadian-Greenland Arctic
abstract:
Tropical Indo-western Pacific forcing expedites warming in the northern Canadian-Greenland Arctic 
 Since the beginning of modern satellite monitoring around 1980, near-surface and tropospheric temperatures in the northern Canadian-Greenland Arctic have substantially warmed, with magnitudes comparable to those in the pan-Arctic. However, the main causes of this marked regional warming and its magnitude in future projections remain debated because of large inter-model spread across historical and future periods. Here, using a hierarchy of pacemaker experiments in which regional sea surface temperature anomalies are nudged toward observations, we reveal that the tropical Indo-western Pacific (IOWP) forcing amplifies warming in northern Canada and Greenland through the IOWP-Arctic teleconnection. Anomalous tropical IOWP warming remotely triggers enhanced subsidence and reduced total cloud cover, increasing incoming shortwave radiation and, consequently, near-surface and tropospheric temperature warming. Further, by observationally constraining future projected warming magnitudes with recent tropical IOWP warming trends, the upper bounds (95th percentile values) of near-term (2026–2055 minus 1981–2010) warming magnitudes in the northern Canadian-Greenland Arctic and pan-Arctic decrease by ~19.8% and ~18.3%, respectively, under the high-emission scenario. Our results highlight the potential of the tropical IOWP warm pool to enable reliable Arctic warming projections.

title: Sources of skillful seasonal forecasts of springtime CONUS tornado activity
abstract:
Sources of skillful seasonal forecasts of springtime CONUS tornado activity 
 Despite progress in continental United States (CONUS) tornado forecasting, operational seasonal outlooks remain challenging due to intrinsic predictability limits. While previous studies link the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) to spring tornado frequency, relying on single tropical indices misses crucial regional variability. Here, we present a novel hybrid dynamical-statistical framework that introduces a paradigm for long-lead predictability. Utilizing retrospective forecasts from NOAA/GFDL’s state-of-the-art SPEAR model, we demonstrate for the first time that a strategic selection of global sea surface temperature modes yields highly useful, skillful predictions with lead times approaching 4 months. Dominant predictable patterns are rooted in transitioning ENSO phases, the Pacific Meridional Mode, and the trend-associated Caribbean High. Unlike conventional predictors, our framework filters internal noise and captures high-wavenumber anomalies. These findings carry substantial implications for climate services, bridging the gap between weather forecasting and seasonal risk management.

title: Deep-learning climate emulator ACE2 reveals a global decrease in 15th-century tropical cyclone frequency under El Niño-like sea surface temperatures
abstract:
Deep-learning climate emulator ACE2 reveals a global decrease in 15th-century tropical cyclone frequency under El Niño-like sea surface temperatures 
 The relatively short modern observational record limits our understanding of the relationship between global tropical cyclone (TC) frequency and sea surface temperature (SST), resulting in uncertain future TC projections. Using novel deep-learning-based past-millennium simulations with the Ai2 Climate Emulator version 2 (ACE2), we provide insight into the connections between SSTs and TCs. ACE2 simulations reveal that the Atlantic and global tropical cyclone numbers decreased in the 15th Century under an El Niño-like SST pattern, consistent with the high-resolution dynamical climate model HiRAM, and Atlantic sediment proxies. Global TC frequency decreased mainly due to stronger vertical wind shear and the drier midtroposphere as the Hadley circulation strengthened. Conversely, global TC frequency would increase under a La Niña-like SST pattern, as shown in idealized SST experiments with ACE2. This study demonstrates an exciting opportunity to examine TC-climate interactions using deep-learning-based paleoclimate simulations and highlights the need to constrain future projections of SST patterns to accurately estimate TC frequency.

title: Distinct drivers control trace metal distributions through the Atlantic Ocean
abstract:
Transport through water masses formed in high latitudes can explain 60–90% of dissolved trace metal distributions and higher than 75% of trace metal inventories in the interior of the Atlantic Ocean, based on water mass analysis. 
 Trace metals (TMs) including iron, manganese, cobalt, nickel, copper, zinc, cadmium, and lead have important biogeochemical roles in the ocean. However, the controlling factors of TM distributions have not yet been quantified and investigated on an ocean scale. Here we take a holistic approach to demonstrate that transport through water masses formed in high latitudes can explain 60–90% of dissolved TM distributions and >75% of TM inventories in the interior Atlantic. Water mass signatures were slightly modified by sinking organic matter remineralization mainly for iron, cobalt, nickel, cadmium, scavenging removal for iron, manganese, cobalt, lead, and hydrothermal inputs for iron and manganese. Our approach allowed prediction of the baseline TM distributions through the Atlantic at high spatial resolution. Through quantification, our findings emphasize the important role of large-scale oceanic circulation in determining global TM distributions once the water mass endmembers are set, despite the distinctive geochemical behaviors of the assessed TMs. Climate-related changes in a future ocean that impact endmember concentrations or relative water mass contributions may therefore perturb downstream TM inventories and ultimately affect ocean productivity and ocean carbon pump. title: Social vulnerability amplifies global inequality in urban heat risk
abstract:
Urban heat risk increased worldwide during 2000–2019, with growth in the Global South nearly five times that in the Global North, and conventional approaches underestimate North-South inequality by nearly 65 percent, according to an analysis of 1,029 global cities. 
 Assessing urban heat risk is essential for developing heat adaptation and mitigation strategies. A key challenge in global-scale risk assessments is the common assumption of spatially homogeneous social vulnerability, often due to data constraints. Yet, the extent to which this assumption underestimates global climate inequality remains unclear. Here, we conduct a comparative heat risk assessment across 1,029 global cities during 2000–2019 by introducing a multidimensional social vulnerability index. Results reveal increasing urban heat risk worldwide, with the upward trend in the Global South nearly five-fold that in the Global North. We demonstrate that the traditional homogeneous assumption leads to a nearly 65% underestimation of North-South inequality in long-term heat risk. Furthermore, intraregional inequality measured by the Gini index is larger within the Global North and is underestimated by nearly 15% under the homogeneous assumption. Our study quantifies systematic bias in existing global heat risk assessments, providing a foundation for advancing climate justice in a rapidly warming world. title: Episodic isolation of the Arctic Mediterranean from the North Atlantic during late Pleistocene glacials
abstract:
Highly dynamic coupling between the Arctic Mediterranean and the North Atlantic during late Pleistocene glaciations; as shown using Beryllium isotopes from sediment cores from the Arctic Ocean, the Nordic Seas and the North Atlantic. 
 It has been proposed that the Arctic Ocean and Nordic Seas (“the Arctic Mediterranean”) were not only episodically covered by an ice shelf during late Pleistocene glaciations, but disconnected from the North Atlantic and filled with freshwater. Originally based on the widespread occurrence of marine sediments with intervals barren of 230Thxs (a function of salinity) and low in cosmogenic 10Be (interpreted as ice cover), this interpretation is highly debated. Alternative explanations state that sediment pulses could instead have diluted both isotopes. Here, we trace the connection between the Arctic Mediterranean and the North Atlantic using reactive 10Be/9Be, a water mass tracer resilient to sedimentation variations. We find uniformly low 10Be/9Be that coincide with the 230Thxs-minima and more than one order of magnitude below the coeval North Atlantic, consistent with an isolated Arctic Mediterranean. Our findings suggest a highly dynamic coupling between the Arctic Mediterranean and the North Atlantic, opening questions about its impact on global climate. title: Impact of climate change on the photovoltaic power potential in Sweden across 21st century
abstract:
Future climate change is projected to increase solar photovoltaic power generation in Sweden by about 5% compared to historical periods, while optimized panel tilt can boost output by 3 to 6%; according to a validated installation model incorporating air temperature, solar radiation, and snow conditions across four cities under future climate scenarios. 
 Solar photovoltaic generation strongly relies on weather conditions, which will be affected by future climate change. Traditional methods for estimating photovoltaic generation potential often overlook detailed installation factors and snow impacts, leading to inaccuracies in high-latitude areas. We assess future photovoltaic system performance in Sweden using a validated photovoltaic installation model that incorporates air temperature, radiation and snow conditions. Applying this model to four Swedish cities under low- and high-emission climate change scenarios and three climate simulations, we project an approximate 5% increase in photovoltaic generation relative to the historical period with optimal installation angle. The combined effects of air temperature and snowfall are as crucial as solar radiation for photovoltaic generation in Sweden, so the photovoltaic generation change will be relatively limited by 2100. Optimized tilt angles are obtained for all the four cities, which could increase photovoltaic generation by 3-6% compared to the commercial angle. The findings also provide valuable insights into photovoltaic potential in a changing climate. title: Revisiting the urban past virtually to enhance well-being for older adults
abstract:
As development progresses, urban landmarks may be lost to history, resulting in the disconnection and isolation of older adults from their contemporary city. Huang and colleagues virtually reconstructed immersive past urban scenes from Hong Kong to understand the physiological and psychological effects and support mental health for aging populations. 
 Cities are more than physical infrastructure; they are dynamic repositories of collective memories. Rapid urbanization, however, threatens to erase cherished landmarks, severing the connection between communities and their history. To address this loss, we created immersive virtual heritage environments based on CITY IN TIME, a digital platform that uses immersive technology to reconstruct 44 iconic Hong Kong landmarks as they existed between 1900 and 1970 from archival sources. Here we demonstrate that a virtual experience of historical Hong Kong significantly enhanced memory recall, reduced stress and increased social connectedness in older adults, supported by consistent physiological and psychological measures. Semi-structured interviews further revealed the multidimensional nature of urban memory, encompassing both tangible places and intangible narratives. Taken together, our findings illustrate how urban heritage can safeguard collective memory and foster community well-being, offering a scalable approach to preserving the layered histories that shape inclusive and emotionally resonant cities.
